A2.text:
Rashad and his friend Aysel are on a trip to Shahdag. The mountains are beautiful, but Rashad has a big problem. He is afraid of heights. For him, high places are a nightmare.

Aysel wants to ride the cable car to the top. “Come on, Rashad!” she says. “It is very safe.”

Rashad agrees, but when he sees the glass cabin, he gets cold feet. He does not want to go in. Aysel holds his hand. “I am here with you,” she says.

They sit in the cable car. It goes up, up, up. Rashad looks down at the trees. He is scared stiff. He closes his eyes and holds the seat. Aysel talks to him about funny stories to make him smile.

Finally, they arrive at the top of the mountain. Rashad opens his eyes. The view is amazing. He is very happy. He did it!

They walk to a small café to drink tea. Suddenly, Aysel jumps up and screams.

“What is it?” Rashad asks.

Aysel points at the table. “A spider!” she cries.

Rashad laughs. He takes a napkin, picks up the tiny spider, and puts it outside. “Do not worry,” he says. “I can protect you from spiders, and you can protect me from heights.”

questions.q: What is the main idea of the story?
options: Rashad and Aysel hate the mountains
A spider bites Aysel in the cable car
Rashad leaves his friend and goes home
Rashad is afraid of heights but helps his friend who is afraid of spiders
questions.why: The story is about Rashad facing his fear of heights and then rescuing Aysel from her fear of a spider.

options: In Baku
At Shahdag
At the beach
In a forest
questions.why: “Rashad and his friend Aysel are on a trip to Shahdag.”

questions.q: What does Aysel do in the cable car to help Rashad?
options: She gives him tea
She tells him to look down
She talks to him about funny stories
She plays music
questions.why: “Aysel talks to him about funny stories to make him smile.”

questions.q: Rashad runs away and does not get in the cable car.
options: True
False
Not given
questions.why: False because the text says, “They sit in the cable car.”

questions.q: Rashad is “scared stiff”. What does this mean?
options: He is extremely frightened
He is very tired
He is hungry
He is very cold
questions.why: He is on a high cable car and he is afraid of heights, so he closes his eyes and holds the seat.

questions.q: Why does Rashad say, “I can protect you from spiders, and you can protect me from heights”?
options: Because he wants to be a policeman
Because Aysel is very strong
Because he brought a lot of napkins
Because they both have different fears and can help each other
questions.why: He realizes they both have things they are afraid of, and they can support each other.

B1.text:
Rashad has always loved the fresh air of the mountains, but he hides one difficult secret: a terrible phobia of heights. Last weekend, he travelled to the beautiful Shahdag resort with his good friend Aysel. The snowy peaks looked absolutely amazing in the morning sun, but Rashad felt a deep anxiety when Aysel pointed at the long cable car.

“Let’s go to the highest restaurant on the mountain!” she said excitedly.

Rashad agreed because he wanted to be brave, but as they stood in the ticket queue, he started to get cold feet. When the doors of the glass cabin finally opened, his heart beat so fast that he thought he was going to have a panic attack.

“I really can’t do this,” he said, stepping back.

Aysel quickly held his arm to reassure him. “You are completely safe, Rashad,” she smiled. “Just look at my face, not out of the window.”

They sat down, and the cable car pulled them high up into the sky. Rashad was scared stiff, but he kept his eyes fixed on Aysel. She told funny stories about their university days and made him laugh. Slowly, his breathing returned to normal. By the time they reached the top, he felt proud. He managed to overcome his fear.

They walked into the mountain café and sat at a wooden table. Suddenly, Aysel jumped out of her chair with a loud scream.

“What happened?” Rashad asked in surprise.

Aysel pointed a shaking finger at the sugar bowl. “Spider!” she cried.

Rashad looked down and saw a tiny, harmless spider. He laughed, picked it up with a napkin, and carried it outside. “Well,” he smiled, returning to his tea. “I guess we all have our own nightmares.”

questions.q: What happens during their trip to Shahdag?
options: They get lost in the mountains
They refuse to ride the cable car
Rashad faces his fear of heights, and then discovers Aysel's fear of spiders
Aysel helps Rashad become a professional mountain climber
questions.why: The story shows Rashad overcoming his phobia with Aysel's help, and then he helps her when she panics over a spider.

questions.q: Why does Rashad agree to go on the cable car at first?
options: He likes the view
He wants to be brave
Aysel pays for him
He wants to drink tea
questions.why: “Rashad agreed because he wanted to be brave...”

questions.q: Rashad started to “get cold feet”. What does this mean?
options: To need warm winter boots
To get angry at a friend
To feel very confident
To suddenly become too nervous to do something you planned
questions.why: He stood in the queue but got so nervous he wanted to step back and not go in.

questions.q: How does Rashad probably feel when he sees Aysel screaming at the spider?
options: Angry that she ruined his tea
Amused because everyone has their own fears
Sad that the spider is hurt
Terrified because he hates spiders too
questions.why: He laughs and says, “I guess we all have our own nightmares,” showing he finds it slightly funny and relatable.

B2.text:
Despite being an adventurous guy who loved hiking, Rashad suffered from acrophobia—an intense and completely irrational fear of heights. Last Saturday, he and his closest friend, Aysel, drove up to the spectacular Shahdag Mountain Resort. The crisp winter air was refreshing, but Rashad’s anxiety spiked the moment Aysel pointed toward the summit.

“We have to ride the gondola to the peak café!” she insisted, her eyes shining with excitement.

Rashad knew he had to face his fears eventually, so he forced a smile and bought a ticket. However, waiting on the platform proved to be a powerful trigger. As the transparent glass cabin swung into the station, his palms began to sweat. He was ready to get cold feet, convinced a full-blown panic attack was only seconds away.

“I don’t think I can go through with this,” he muttered, backing away from the doors.

Sensing his distress, Aysel gently grabbed his elbow to reassure him. “Hey, look at me. The engineering is flawless. Just focus on our conversation, and whatever you do, don’t look down.”

He stepped inside, feeling scared stiff as the cabin lurched upward, leaving the solid ground far below. Aysel instantly launched into an entertaining story about her crazy office manager in Baku. Her chatter was a perfect distraction. By the time they docked at the mountain station, Rashad’s racing heart had steadied. He stepped out into the snow, genuinely thrilled that he had managed to overcome his phobia.

They found a cosy table inside the timber-framed café. Rashad was just pouring them both a cup of hot black tea when Aysel suddenly shrieked and leapt away from the table, nearly knocking over her chair.

Rashad jumped up. “What’s wrong? Are you hurt?”

Trembling, she pointed at the edge of the sugar bowl. “Spider!” she gasped.

Rashad leaned in and spotted a spider no bigger than a breadcrumb. Amused by the irony, he scooped the tiny creature onto a napkin and released it out the window.

“Don’t worry,” he chuckled, sitting back down. “It seems we both have our own irrational triggers.”

words.phrase: leaving the solid ground far below

questions.q: What is the central theme of the story?
options: Both friends discovering they have their own specific anxieties to overcome
A mountain hike that goes completely wrong
Why spiders are a dangerous threat in winter
The brilliant engineering of modern cable cars
questions.why: Rashad faces his acrophobia, and Aysel immediately after exhibits arachnophobia, showing they both have irrational fears.

options: She played a game on her phone
She told an entertaining story about her office manager
She pointed out the beautiful snowy peaks
She gave him a cup of hot black tea
questions.why: “Aysel instantly launched into an entertaining story about her crazy office manager in Baku.”

questions.q: How big was the spider that terrified Aysel?
options: As big as a tea cup
Too small to see
The size of a napkin
No bigger than a breadcrumb

questions.q: Rashad refused to ride the gondola and waited for Aysel at the bottom.
options: True
False
Not given
questions.why: False because the text states, “He stepped inside, feeling scared stiff...” and made it to the top.

questions.q: Waiting on the platform proved to be a powerful “trigger”. What is a trigger in this context?

Something that causes a strong emotional or physical reaction
A tool used to buy tickets
A person who works at the mountain resort

questions.q: Why does Rashad chuckle at the end of the story?
options: He finds it funny that his brave friend is terrified of something so small
He thinks Aysel's story about the office manager is funny
He is happy that the tea is still hot
He wants to scare her with the spider again
questions.why: He is “amused by the irony” that Aysel, who fearlessly guided him through the sky, is terrified of a tiny spider.
